status: CORRECTED estimate. Rotation is unchanged/trustworthy; t_z is fixed. The exact range bias (hence exact t_z) still needs a tape measurement of the radar's fore-aft setback to finalize.

why_corrected.defect_1_outlier: capture i=23 is a bad elevation point: p_radar=[2.395,-0.021,+0.511] — the only positive radar-Z in the set (all others -0.08..-0.77). 3-D residual 1356 mm vs 167 mm median (8x). The radar's weak elevation axis flipped sign. It was wrongly kept as an inlier (node reported 31/31). Removed here.
why_corrected.defect_2_range_bias: range_fit cam_r = 0.971*radar_r - 0.108 m: a ~-9 cm range bias remains AFTER the 1.039 scale. The radar boresight is 96.6% aligned with camera +Z, so this bias projects ~-8.7 cm into t_z, inflating it from a true ~-2..-7 cm to the recorded -0.1721. Corrected by applying r' = 0.979*r - 0.09 on the (already 1.039-scaled) ranges.

caveats: The range bias here is radar1-specific (radar2's range fit was +0.089, opposite sign — so it is NOT the reflector phase center; each radar has its own range calibration). The exact -9 cm was fit from these poses and is coupled with the reflector offset; the precise t_z depends on the true range calibration. To finalize: tape-measure the radar1 fore-aft setback behind the ZED lens, set radar_range_bias_m so the solved t_z matches it, and re-run. Then this file can be promoted to the radar1 result.
how_i23_slipped_through: The reject gate (reject_sigma=4.0) compares the RMS-across-axes normalized residual = chi/sqrt(k). i=23 was range -3.82sigma and elevation +3.83sigma (azimuth clean 0.15) -> chi 5.41, but chi/sqrt(3)=3.12 < 4.0, so the clean azimuth axis averaged it under the gate. FIX (new, opt-in): set reject_axis_sigma:=3.5 on the re-run — a per-axis cap that drops any match whose single worst axis exceeds 3.5sigma, catching i=23 (max axis 3.83). Default reject_axis_sigma=0 keeps existing behavior unchanged.
